Name: True Rune - Powerful Schedule Patcher
Author: Riou0903
Description:
[size=5][b]True Rune: Schedule Director — Conditional NPC Schedules[/b][/size]
[size=3][i]Where they go. When they go. Why they go. All in JSON.[/i][/size]

[size=4][b]The pitch[/b][/size]

Drop [b]one JSON file per NPC[/b] and give them daily routines that react to the world: the season, the weather, who you've gotten close to, whether you're dating or married, which story events you've seen. Pick the right route automatically, rotate between options for variety, and [b]fall back to vanilla the moment your conditions don't match[/b] — all without counting forward-slashes in raw schedule strings.

True Rune: Schedule Director picks the best-matching routine through a [b]Chain-of-Responsibility resolver[/b]: every condition narrows the candidates, then the winner is chosen by [color=#9ACD32]priority → specificity → rotation[/color]. The game still does all the path-finding — you just describe the day.

[size=4][b]Works alongside Content Patcher[/b][/size]

Both can edit [color=#9ACD32]Characters/schedules/*[/color], but at different layers. Content Patcher gives you raw schedule-string control with its own conditions. Schedule Director gives you a [b]structured, runtime resolver[/b] with cross-NPC logic vanilla can't express — and it writes its result at [b]Late[/b] priority, so when your rule matches it wins, and when it doesn't, your Content Patcher / vanilla schedule is left completely untouched.

[size=4][b]What you get[/b][/size]

[list]
[*][b]One file per NPC, many routines.[/b] Each candidate is a full day's route plus the conditions under which it applies.[/*]
[*][b]Conditions vanilla can't do.[/b] Gate a route on hearts with [i]other[/i] NPCs, on dating/marriage status, on dance partner, on events seen, on mail flags (AND / OR / forbidden), on weather, season, weekday, and day/year ranges — combined freely.[/*]
[*][b]Priority + rotation.[/b] Highest-priority match wins. Tie? Equally-specific routes rotate day to day in a shuffled round-robin, so your NPC doesn't do the exact same thing forever.[/*]
[*][b]Named location points.[/b] Say [color=#9ACD32]"point": "beach_pier_1"[/color] instead of memorizing tile coordinates. Ships a starter registry of proven-walkable spots; add your own in a [color=#9ACD32]points.json[/color].[/*]
[*][b]Prioritize-over-vanilla with automatic fallback.[/b] No match = no edit = vanilla behaves normally. Festival days are left alone by default.[/*]
[*][b]No Harmony.[/b] Pure SMAPI asset pipeline. The game parses and path-finds your route exactly like any other schedule.[/*]
[*][b]Part of a toolkit.[/b] One content pack can ship schedules [i]and[/i] events [i]and[/i] dialogue under a single [color=#9ACD32]TrueRune/[/color] folder — each True Rune framework scans the subfolder it owns.[/*]
[/list]
[size=4][b]Concrete comparison — same idea, vanilla vs. TRS[/b][/size]

[b]Vanilla schedule string[/b] — one giant slash-delimited line per key, and there's no way to say "only when the player is close to both Emily and Penny":

[code]
"summer": "900 HaleyHouse 6 5 0/1000 Beach 27 34 2 haley_beach_towel/1700 Town 47 87 2/2200 HaleyHouse 1 5 3 haley_sleep"[/code]
[b]The same day in TRS[/b] — named fields, named points, and a condition block:

[code]
{
"npc": "Haley",
"schedules": [
{
"id": "summer_sunny_beach",
"priority": 20,
"conditions": { "seasons": ["summer"], "weather": ["sunny"] },
"points": [
{ "time": 900,  "point": "haley_home_door" },
{ "time": 1000, "point": "beach_towel", "animation": "haley_beach_towel" },
{ "time": 1700, "point": "town_plaza" },
{ "time": 2200, "point": "haley_home_bed", "animation": "haley_sleep" }
]
}
]
}[/code]
[size=4][b]Tutorial — layered routines that react to your save[/b][/size]

Add more candidates to the same file. Higher priority wins; the resolver falls through to the next match automatically.

[code]
"schedules": {

"_married": [
{
"id": "married_morning_walk",
"priority": 40,
"conditions": { "is_spouse": true, "weather": ["sunny"] },
"points": [
{ "time": 1000, "point": "beach_entrance" },
{ "time": 1800, "point": "haley_home_couch" }
]
}
],

"_close_to_the_girls": [
{
"id": "double_date_prep",
"priority": 30,
"conditions": {
"seasons": ["summer"], "weather": ["sunny"],
"npc_heart_conditions": [
{ "npc": "Emily", "min_heart": 6 },
{ "npc": "Penny", "min_heart": 6 }
]
},
"points": [
{ "time": 900,  "point": "town_plaza" },
{ "time": 1100, "point": "beach_pier_1" },
{ "time": 1700, "point": "saloon_bar" },
{ "time": 2330, "point": "haley_home_bed", "animation": "haley_sleep" }
]
}
],

"_default_rotation": [
{ "id": "default_museum", "priority": 0, "points": [ { "time": 1000, "point": "town_museum_steps" }, { "time": 2200, "point": "haley_home_bed", "animation": "haley_sleep" } ] },
{ "id": "default_pierre", "priority": 0, "points": [ { "time": 1000, "point": "pierre_shop_floor" }, { "time": 2200, "point": "haley_home_bed", "animation": "haley_sleep" } ] }
]

}[/code]
[b]What that does:[/b]
[list]
[*]Married + sunny → the morning walk (priority 40).[/*]
[*]Otherwise, summer + sunny + 6♥ with [b]both[/b] Emily and Penny → the day out (priority 30) — a cross-NPC condition vanilla simply can't express.[/*]
[*]Otherwise, the two priority-0 defaults tie, so Haley [b]alternates[/b] between the museum and Pierre's day to day.[/*]
[*]Nothing matches at all? TRS writes nothing and Haley follows her vanilla schedule.[/*]
[/list]
The grouping keys ([color=#9ACD32]_married[/color], [color=#9ACD32]_seasonal[/color], …) are just for collapsing sections in your editor — they're ignored at runtime. You can also use a flat array.

[size=4][b]Named location points[/b][/size]

Reference reusable spots by key; ship your own in [color=#9ACD32]TrueRune/schedules/points.json[/color]:

[code]
{
"points": {
"beach_pier_1": { "location": "Beach", "x": 38, "y": 36, "facing": "down" }
}
}[/code]
Your points merge on top of the built-in registry. Run [color=#9ACD32]rune_sched_points[/color] in-game to list every key that's loaded.

[size=4][b]It just works the moment you install it[/b][/size]

The framework ships a [b]smoke-test schedule for Haley[/b], gated behind a flag so it never touches a real save until you ask. Load a game and run [color=#9ACD32]rune_sched_smoke Haley[/color] — she heads to the beach, confirming everything is wired up. Run [color=#9ACD32]rune_sched_try Haley[/color] to print the exact schedule string she'll follow.

[size=4][b]Quick start for authors[/b][/size]

[code]
MySchedulePack/
├── manifest.json    (ContentPackFor: "Riou.TrueRune.Schedules")
└── TrueRune/
└── schedules/
├── Haley.json
└── points.json[/code]
[b]manifest.json:[/b]

[code]
{
"Name": "My Schedule Pack",
"Author": "You",
"Version": "1.0.0",
"Description": "New routines for Haley.",
"UniqueID": "You.MySchedulePack",
"ContentPackFor": { "UniqueID": "Riou.TrueRune.Schedules", "MinimumVersion": "1.0.0" }
}[/code]
Drop the folder into [color=#9ACD32]Stardew Valley/Mods/[/color] → launch → sleep once. That's the whole loop.

[size=4][b]Condition reference[/b][/size]

[list]
[*][color=#9ACD32]required_AND_flags[/color] / [color=#9ACD32]required_OR_flags[/color] / [color=#9ACD32]forbidden_flags[/color] — mail flags[/*]
[*][color=#9ACD32]required_seen_events[/color] — event IDs in eventsSeen[/*]
[*][color=#9ACD32]min_heart[/color] / [color=#9ACD32]max_heart[/color] — hearts with this NPC[/*]
[*][color=#9ACD32]npc_heart_conditions[/color] — hearts with [b]other[/b] NPCs[/*]
[*][color=#9ACD32]seasons[/color] / [color=#9ACD32]days_of_week[/color] / [color=#9ACD32]min_day[/color]–[color=#9ACD32]max_day[/color] / [color=#9ACD32]min_year[/color]–[color=#9ACD32]max_year[/color][/*]
[*][color=#9ACD32]weather[/color] — sunny / rainy / stormy / snowy / windy[/*]
[*][color=#9ACD32]is_spouse[/color] / [color=#9ACD32]is_dating[/color] / [color=#9ACD32]is_dance_partner[/color][/*]
[/list]
[size=4][b]Point reference[/b][/size]

[list]
[*][color=#9ACD32]time[/color] — military, no colon (900 = 9am). [color=#9ACD32]arrive_by[/color] adds the "arrive by" prefix.[/*]
[*][color=#9ACD32]point[/color] — registry key — or inline [color=#9ACD32]location[/color] + [color=#9ACD32]x[/color] + [color=#9ACD32]y[/color][/*]
[*][color=#9ACD32]facing[/color] — up/right/down/left (or 0–3)[/*]
[*][color=#9ACD32]animation[/color] — animationDescriptions key ([color=#9ACD32]haley_beach_towel[/color], [color=#9ACD32]square_5_3[/color], any [color=#9ACD32]*sleep*[/color])[/*]
[*][color=#9ACD32]dialogue[/color] — location-dialogue token[/*]
[*][color=#9ACD32]location: "bed"[/color] — go home and sleep[/*]
[/list]
Full schema + a complete worked pack ([color=#9ACD32]samples/Sample-HaleyBeachDayPack/[/color]) ship inside the download. Author guide: [color=#9ACD32]docs/SCHEDULE_AUTHORING.md[/color].

[size=4][b]Install[/b][/size]

[list=1]
[*]Install [url=https://smapi.io/]SMAPI 4.0+[/url][/*]
[*][i]Recommended:[/i] [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/5098]Generic Mod Config Menu[/url] for the in-game settings page[/*]
[*]Drop the unzipped folder into [color=#9ACD32]Stardew Valley/Mods/[/color][/*]
[*]Install any content pack that requires this framework[/*]
[/list]
[size=4][b]Console commands (prefix rune_sched_)[/b][/size]

· [color=#9ACD32]rune_sched_list [NPC][/color] — NPCs with schedules, or every candidate for one NPC
· [color=#9ACD32]rune_sched_try <NPC>[/color] — which candidate wins now + the compiled schedule string
· [color=#9ACD32]rune_sched_apply [NPC][/color] — force re-resolution + reapply right now
· [color=#9ACD32]rune_sched_points [filter][/color] — list known location points
· [color=#9ACD32]rune_sched_reload[/color] — re-scan every JSON from disk and rebuild
· [color=#9ACD32]rune_sched_smoke [NPC][/color] — enable the built-in smoke test and reapply
· (vanilla) [color=#9ACD32]debug seenMail <flag> [false][/color] — toggle a flag to test gating

Type [color=#9ACD32]help rune_sched_<name>[/color] in the SMAPI console for usage.

[size=4][b]C# API[/b][/size]

[code]
var api = Helper.ModRegistry.GetApi<IScheduleDirectorApi>("Riou.TrueRune.Schedules");

// Contribute routes at runtime from your own mod
api.RegisterSchedules("Haley", myEntries, ModManifest.UniqueID);

// Preview what would apply right now
api.TryResolve("Haley", out string compiled);[/code]
[size=4][b]Compatibility & permissions[/b][/size]

SMAPI 4.0+ / Stardew Valley 1.6+. Stacks alongside Content Patcher schedule edits and custom-NPC frameworks. [b]MIT licensed[/b] — use as a dependency without asking, fork freely, translations welcome.

Manifest.Name: True Rune: Schedule Director
Manifest.Description: Conditional NPC schedule engine. Authors drop a JSON file per character to override vanilla daily routines with priority, rotation, and flag/heart/cross-NPC-heart/date/season/weather/relationship/event-seen conditions. Prioritizes over vanilla and Content Patcher when a rule matches, and falls back to them when none does.
